subject: Proposal: SLA uplift + overage shielding for renewal – Sentinel Analytics
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@sentinelanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, k arthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Renewal: proposed SLA uplift and capacity plan

Hi Maria,

As Sentinel's renewal is approaching (12/01), I wanted to share a concise proposal to address the two items you've raised on our last call: a tighter latency SLO for the inference endpoints and protection against overage surprises during high-demand events.

Key points in the attached proposal (redwood-sla-proposal-v2.pdf):
- Premium SLA option: 99.95% monthly uptime, 100ms p95 on our dedicated endpoint configuration during business-peak windows.
- Overage shielding: pre-agreed burst blocks and a one-time buffer credit to cover unexpected spikes in month 1 and 2 of the renewal term.
- Support: 24x7 priority incident routing with 30-minute escalation to on-call for Sev-1, and monthly health reviews with a named TAM.

If this direction looks good, I can circulate a mutual action plan and a DocuSign draft of the updated terms. Would you be open to a 30-minute alignment call the week of 10/27 to finalize trade-offs (latency vs price vs capacity)?

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood-sla-proposal-v2.pdf

From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@sentinelanalytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Sentinel Analytics Procurement <procurement@sentinelanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal: proposed SLA uplift and capacity plan

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the quick outline. A couple of clarifying questions before we loop procurement in formally:

1) That 100ms p95 number — is that for our existing model profile with current prompt sizes (avg 350 tokens) or only for the trimmed prompt profile you mentioned on the demo? We need the SLO to reflect our actual workload.
2) On overage shielding: what triggers consumption of the buffer credit? Is it strictly token-count overage, or do we include inference-minute (GPU runtime) overages as well?

Procurement is CC'd; once we have specifics I expect they'll want the mutual action plan and a PO cadence. Also, could you put high-level pricing delta (ballpark %) in the plan so finance can quickly pre-approve?

— Maria
VP, AI Systems
Sentinel Analytics
maria.garcia@sentinelanalytics.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@sentinelanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, k arthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Oct 2025 10:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal: proposed SLA uplift and capacity plan

Hi Maria — good questions. Short answers up front and detail below.

- 100ms p95: measured against your current profile (avg prompt 350 tokens, avg generation 75 tokens) on a dedicated instance profile we profiled during the pilot. We'll include the performance baseline in the proposal so it's explicit.
- Buffer credit: covers token-based overages and GPU-runtime overages that exceed committed capacity in a given billing period; it won't apply to deliberate throttling events.
- Pricing delta: premium SLA + overage shielding is estimated at ~18–22% uplift over your current committed plan (range reflects final capacity commit).

I've attached an updated PDF with a small performance appendix and a sample mutual action plan. If procurement needs hard numbers we can move to a short call to confirm exact capacity tiers.

Proposed next steps:
1) Agree on the capacity tier (x-dedicated GPUs) and confirm baseline token profile — I can send a short telemetry extract.
2) Procurement confirms PO cadence and any contractual constraints (net-45/60, export controls).
3) We draft final terms and circulate via DocuSign.

Would you be available for a 30-min sync on Thu 10/30 or Mon 11/03?

Regards,
Hannah

Attachment: redwood-sla-proposal-v2.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, k arthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 23 Oct 2025 08:11:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: proposed SLA uplift and capacity plan

Looping in Karthik and Vanessa for pricing/ops alignment. Suggest we offer the following to keep the deal moving:
- 3-month ramp credit equal to 15% of the first quarter's invoices to reduce immediate overage concern.
- Named TAM and twice-monthly health calls for the first 90 days.
- A one-time performance validation window in which SLA credits are held in abeyance to validate the baseline (we document metrics).

Karthik — can you fast-track an ops feasibility check on the dedicated pool and confirm whether the 100ms p95 is realistic across the US-East region under your capacity plans?

Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Procurement <procurement@sentinelanalytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@sentinelanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2025 16:45:00 -0400
Subject: Sentinel Analytics — proposed redlines for renewal terms

Hi Hannah and Maria,

Procurement has reviewed the draft terms. A few redlines we need addressed before we can proceed to PO: 
- Term length: request a 12-month commitment rather than 24 months given uncertain Q1 usage.
- Liquidated damages cap: lower the maximum SLA credit cap from 6 months' spend to 3 months.
- Data residency: confirm that event logs used for SLA calculations will be retained for 12 months and that the audit trail is exportable for our compliance team.

Also attaching a prioritized mutual action plan template — please populate responsibilities and target dates.

Best,
Sentinel Analytics Procurement Team
procurement@sentinelanalytics.com

Attachment referenced: procurement-redlines.docx

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Procurement <procurement@sentinelanalytics.com>, Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@sentinelanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, k arthik.iyer@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Oct 2025 09:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sentinel Analytics — proposed redlines for renewal terms

Thanks — I populated the mutual action plan and attached it (mutual-action-plan-sentinel.xlsx). Responses inline to the redlines: 

- Term length: we can accommodate a 12-month commitment with an option to extend at the same rates at 9 months; we'll include a renewal-option clause.
- SLA credit cap: we can reduce the cap to 3 months' spend for this renewal given the preferred ramp credit we offered.
- Data residency & audit: logs will be retained for 12 months and we will provide an exportable CSV/Parquet for your compliance review. We'll add that to the addendum.

Next steps: I've scheduled a 30-minute alignment call for Mon 11/03 at 10:00am ET to finalize outstanding items and circulate the DocuSign envelope afterward. I'll include the DocuSign draft (docusign-draft-terms-2025.pdf) in the post-call email.

Hannah

Attachment: mutual-action-plan-sentinel.xlsx

From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@sentinelanalytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@sentinelanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 11:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sentinel Analytics — proposed redlines for renewal terms

Hannah — thanks for the updates and for taking the mutual action plan. The procurement redlines look reasonable with the 3-month cap and the 12-month term. We are good to proceed with the call on 11/03 and would like the DocuSign envelope right after the meeting if possible.

Please ensure the DocuSign has the PO number field and our internal signatory block.

Thanks,
Maria
